**The tenth** — taking counsel of the intellect in everything that caprice whispers in his heart, and acting on its judgment to the exclusion of the judgment of caprice.

As for the works that are completed by the purification for God when one undertakes them — they are the works of obedience aimed at the satisfaction of God (exalted be He): namely, the totality of the manifest obligations upon the limbs, in which the doer's directing of them to other than God is possible, so that his aim becomes self-adornment for people by them, the seeking of their honor for him, and their praise of him for performing them.

As for the duties of the heart — neither ostentation nor love of honor and praise is possible in them for whoever has bound himself to anything of them, since people have no knowledge of that from him; the one who undertakes them aims by them at the face of the One who is informed of them, namely God (exalted be He) only, as He said: "I, the Lord, am one who tries the heart, who searches the kidneys" (Jeremiah 17:10); and He said: "The hidden things belong to the Lord our God, but the revealed things belong to us and to our children" (Deuteronomy 29:28).
